title: Oscillatory provisioning caused by probe synchronization — mitigation & follow-up
creator: Anika Rao
description: Summary: On 2026-02-26 we observed repeated short-lived capacity swings in the inference fleet for a set of CPU-backed controller nodes handling KEDA-scaled Redis stream triggers. The autoscaler oscillated between scale-up and rapid scale-down windows causing elevated tail latency for a subset of customer traffic (5-10% of requests experienced 2x latency for ~20 minutes). This ticket captures the postmortem, root-cause analysis, and action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-26 03:12 UTC: Alert from SLO monitor (p95 latency drift) triggered for region us-west-2. Incident channel created.
2026-02-26 03:17 UTC: Ops team observed repeated replica churn on the KEDA-managed deployment: 4 -> 8 -> 3 -> 7 -> 3 over 18 minutes.
2026-02-26 03:25 UTC: Service owners forced a temporary minReplicas=6 to stabilize traffic while investigation proceeded (hotfix).

2026-02-26 04:00 UTC: Engineering identified a pattern of near-simultaneous probe/metric flushes causing bursts in the percentile-based scaler. Root-cause hypothesis documented and validated with synthetic traffic replay.
2026-02-26 06:10 UTC: Hotfix reverted after KEDA cooldown and probe jitter patch deployed to a canary subset; metrics normalized.
root_cause: The KEDA Redis stream scaler configuration used a short scrape window and percentile-based rate estimation. Metrics from multiple pods were flushed on aligned intervals (aligned telemetry batching from our metrics exporter), which produced synchronized spikes in the scaler's input. The HPA branch that uses average CPU and KEDA's external scaler both reacted to the same transient signal; combined, they caused overshoot and immediate downscale once the telemetry window slid. In short: telemetry flush alignment + aggressive percentile thresholding + insufficient scaler damping = oscillatory provisioning.
impact: Customer-facing: transient tail-latency increase for ~20 minutes affecting 5-10% of requests in us-west-2. Operational: increased pod churn, higher GPU/CPU allocation churn leading to added cost and noisy alerting (false positives). No data loss or security impact detected.
investigation_notes: Metric investigation revealed >90% of scale events occurred within 5s windows across multiple replicas — unlikely under normal traffic pattern.
Replaying request traces with time-shifted telemetry eliminated the synchronized spikes, confirming flush alignment as a driver.
Heap of exporter batching code had an optimization added in 2025 that aligned flushes to 5s boundaries; this coincided with introduction of a percentile estimator in scaler config last quarter.
HPA and KEDA metrics were not strictly isolated: both used overlapping signals and did not have inter-scaler backoff rules.
Canary patch that added random jitter to telemetry flush reduced simultaneous peaks in synthetic tests.
decisions: Immediate: add small jitter to metrics exporter flush schedule and increase KEDA stabilization window from 30s to 90s (rolled to canary within 2 hours).
Short-term: introduce a de-duplication/backoff layer in the cluster autoscaler controller that rate-limits scale-down operations when multiple scale signals arrive within a short window.
Medium-term: revise scaler configuration defaults to favor 'damped' scaling (gradual ramp-down) for redis-stream and external scalers handling bursty workloads.
Long-term: standardize signal ownership — create a single canonical scaling policy for each workload to avoid competing scalers (HPA vs KEDA).
action_items: ENG-A1: Patch metrics exporter to apply randomized jitter to flush interval (0-4s) and ship in runtime-1.20. Owner: Mateo Kim. Due: 2026-03-07. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5678
ENG-A2: Increase KEDA scaler stabilization window and cooldown defaults; update helm chart values. Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-03-09. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-charts/pull/412
ENG-A3: Implement 'scale-down rate limiter' in autoscaler controller to prevent >50% downscale within 60s. Owner: Luis Ortega. Due: 2026-03-14. Ticket: ENG-438642

ENG-A4: Run 48-hour synthetic replay on staging with varied telemetry jitter and percentile thresholds; collect impact matrices. Owner: SRE Crew. Due: 2026-03-12. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-inference.com/d/autoscale/replay-438271

ENG-A5: Author runbook additions for these oscillation patterns and add a 'temporary minReplicas' mitigation section. Owner: Anika Rao. Due: 2026-03-05. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood-inference.com/display/OPS/Autoscaler+Oscillation+Runbook
ENG-A6: Review open scaler configs across product fleets to identify duplicate signal owners; produce a migration plan to single-signal patterns. Owner: Platform PM (Lena Park). Due: 2026-04-01.
testing_plan: Unit tests covering exporter jitter distribution and edge cases to avoid long-lived drift.
Integration test that simulates 200 pod telemetry alignments and validates that KEDA/HPA combined scaling does not exceed defined thresholds.
Load replay harness to iterate over percentile thresholds (50th/90th/95th) and measure scale decision latency and overshoot frequency.
Safety canary: deploy patched exporter + keda cooldown to 10% of traffic for 48 hours before full rollout.
postmortem_notes: Trade-offs considered: adding jitter reduces metric fidelity for very short-lived spikes but prevents system-level oscillation; we favored stability for production workloads.
We evaluated increasing collector intervals (larger windows) vs jitter — jitter selected because it minimally impacts historical aggregation assumptions.
Cross-team coordination required: metrics team, autoscaler owners, and SRE must align on rollout plan to avoid rolling a change that shifts the problem to another fleet.
This incident highlights a gap in our 'multiple scalers per workload' guardrails — action item ENG-A6 to address.
Estimated cost savings from reducing churn are qualitative but expected to be meaningful under heavy burst patterns (operational CPU/GPU delta reduction).
